b1.summary: All 7 runs kept 15/15 functional tests. Every run failed the T8 test: a credential reproduced by a templated mock response into the body or another header still appears in the stored log, SSE, management stream and runtime log. The models redacted header slots only, which is a security miss. 5/7 runs also accepted a valid secret passed as ?token= on an ordinary (non-streaming) management route. That test is a credential-form/contract rule (the caller holds the real secret), not an access bypass. Rewards are 0.9259-0.963.

b2.note: The T8 echo-redaction test fails in all 7 runs and alone decides 2 of them (0.963). It was added in the 2026-10-20 upgrade.

b3.note: 2 runs are one test short (0.963); the other 5 are two tests short (0.9259).

b4.note: Same pair of tests every time. Runs differ only in whether the query-token rule was also broken.

b5.open_human_question: NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES - should redacting only in the product's logger factory be rejected as a correct fix, and is 'refusing the preflight is an acceptable outcome' scoped to unlisted origins only? Neither is about the decisive tests. FAIRNESS's 'Required: generalize' rewrites (env-prefix sentence, mock-traffic sentence, 'a refused continuing exposure may simply deliver nothing') are still in instruction.md. The echo test is rated 'medium'.

b6.reason: Upstream c420b5a5 accepts the query token only on the SSE endpoint (isSseEndpoint && req.query.token), so the query-token test is covered. Its redaction works on sensitive header entries, and per notes.md neither the published fix nor the previous oracle scrubs a credential echoed into the response body. So T8, which fails in 7/7 runs, is uncovered and survives a lookup.

quotes: the `adminApiAuthToken` option or the `MOCKOON_ADMIN_API_TOKEN` environment setting for the secret, and the `adminApiCorsOrigins` option
A client that cannot set request headers presents the same secret as a `token` query parameter; that form is never a substitute for the header on a request that can carry one.
No record of served traffic that the runtime produces, in any form or for any consumer, may contain the value of a sensitive request or response header.
b7.note: The query-token rule (decisive in 5 runs) is stated almost word for word. 'in any form' points at T8. The models failed both anyway.

b8.note: Full gate PASSED 2026-10-19 (pre-upgrade). Post-upgrade local: oracle 27/27 + 15/15, hardening and alt-fix pass, sf-miss-echo 26/27. Manifest says 'container re-gate pending'.

c1.mechanism: missing authentication on the management API + credential redaction in recorded traffic

c2.pattern: missed value copy outside the redacted slot
c2.note: The decisive gap is the real templating producer, which copies a sensitive header value into the body or another header. Header-name redaction never sees it. The secondary trap (query token on ordinary routes) is a published-fix contract.

d2.evidence: injection.patch adds a /mockoon-admin/logs/stream WebSocket in the server's upgrade handler (it replays transactionLogs and subscribes to transaction-complete, with clean teardown in closeWsServers). It also adds POST env-vars/import, which writes process.env[key] for each key. Both sit next to real siblings (user WS routes, env-var CRUD), use the existing ws dependency and have neutral docs. They were never decisive: all 7 runs fixed both.

e3.why: READY, but NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES is open, and the required generalize edits were not applied

e4.why: T8: a recorded credential leaks through log, stream and runtime output in every run

e5.why: the published fix redacts header slots only; echoed values are not scrubbed

concerns: Very thin margin: rewards 0.926-0.963. One upgrade-added test (T8) decides every run and is the only decider in 2.
The second decisive test is contract-only: a valid secret accepted via query string. Its rule is spelled out in the instruction.
T8's real-world severity is modest: it needs an operator mock template that echoes credentials, and the management API is now authenticated.
Injection contributed nothing: the injected WebSocket stream and bulk import were fixed in every run.
The post-upgrade container re-gate is listed as pending; the gate marker predates the upgrade.
one_line: mockoon: both models locked down the management API and redacted sensitive headers, but none scrubbed a credential that a templated mock response copies into its body. One upgrade-added test decides every run at about 0.93-0.96.
